passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: Amounts are in millions unless specified, except per share data This item generally discusses our 2025 results compared to our 2024 results. Discussions of our 2024 results compared to our 2023 results can be found within Part II, Item 7 of our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2024. Overview Roper Technologies, Inc. (“Roper,” the “Company,” “we,” “our,” or “us”) is a diversified technology company. Roper has a proven, long-term, successful track record of compounding cash flow and increasing shareholder value. We operate market leading businesses that design and develop vertical software and technology enabled products for a variety of defensible niche markets. We pursue consistent and sustainable growth in revenue, earnings, and cash flow by enabling continuous improvement in the operating performance of our existing businesses and by acquiring businesses that offer high value-added software, services, technology-enabled products, and solutions that we believe are capable of realizing growth while maintaining high margins. In November 2022, Roper completed the divestiture of a majority equity stake in its industrial businesses, including its entire historical Process Technologies reportable segment and the industrial businesses within its historical Measurement & Analytical Solutions reportable segment (collectively “Indicor”), to CD&R. Following the sale of the majority equity stake, Roper retained a minority equity interest in Indicor. See Note 9 of the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements included in this Annual Report for additional information regarding Roper’s minority equity interest in Indicor. The financial results of Indicor are reported as discontinued operations for all periods presented. Unless otherwise noted, discussion within Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations relates to continuing operations. Segment Reporting Roper’s segment reporting structure is based on business model and delivery of performance obligations. The three reportable segments are as follows: –Application Software —Aderant, CentralReach, Clinisys, Data Innovations, Deltek, Frontline, IntelliTrans, PowerPlan, Procare, Strata, Transact/CBORD, and Vertafore; –Network Software —ConstructConnect, DAT, Foundry, iPipeline, iTradeNetwork, MHA, SHP, SoftWriters, and Subsplash; –Technology Enabled Products —CIVCO Medical Solutions, FMI, Inovonics, IPA, Neptune, Northern Digital, rf IDEAS, and Verathon. Financial information about our reportable segments is presented in Note 14 of the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements included in this Annual Report. Application of Critical Accounting Policies Our Consolidated Financial Statements are prepared in conformity with generally accepted accounting principles in the United States (“GAAP”). A discussion of our significant accounting policies can also be found in the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements for the year ended December 31, 2025 included in this Annual Report. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: Risks Related to Our Business Operations Our growth strategy includes acquisitions. We may not be able to identify suitable acquisition candidates, complete acquisitions, or integrate acquisitions successfully. Our future rate of growth is highly dependent on our ability to acquire and successfully integrate new businesses. We intend to seek additional acquisition opportunities, both to expand into new markets and to enhance our position in existing markets. There are no assurances, however, that we will be able to successfully identify suitable candidates, negotiate appropriate terms, obtain financing on acceptable terms, complete proposed acquisitions, receive the necessary regulatory approvals (including clearance under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Act in the U.S. and similar antitrust regulations in foreign countries), successfully integrate acquired businesses, or expand into new markets. Once acquired, operations may not achieve anticipated levels of revenues, profitability, or cash flows. Acquisitions involve risks, including difficulties in the integration of the operations, technologies, services, and products of the acquired companies and the diversion of management’s attention from other business concerns. Although our management will endeavor to evaluate the risks inherent in any particular transaction, including but not limited to cybersecurity risks and susceptibility to market disruption from AI or otherwise, there are no assurances that we will properly ascertain all such risks. Acquisitions may involve significant cash expenditures, debt incurrences, equity issuances, and expenses. Difficulties encountered with acquisitions may have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, and results of operations. 9 Our technology is important to our success, and our failure to protect this technology could put us at a competitive disadvantage. Many of our products and services rely on proprietary technology; therefore, we believe that the development and protection of intellectual property rights through patents, copyrights, trade secrets, trademarks, confidentiality agreements, and other contractual provisions are important to the future success of our business. Despite our efforts to protect proprietary rights, unauthorized parties or competitors may copy or otherwise obtain and use our products or technology, including through misappropriation through contractors or other third parties. Actions to enforce these rights may result in substantial costs and diversion of resources, and we make no assurances that any such actions will be successful, particularly given evolving uncertainty regarding protection and ownership of AI-assisted outputs. We rely on information and technology, including third-party cloud computing platforms and other third-party business partners, for many of our business operations which could fail and cause disruption to our business operations. Our business operations are dependent upon information technology networks and systems to securely transmit, process, and store information and to communicate among our locations around the world and with clients, suppliers, and business partners. credit_strengths.text: Roper's revenue and operating income have compounded steadily across the three-year trend, with operating margin well above the Information Technology sector median. This reflects a portfolio of defensible vertical software and technology-enabled products that generate high-margin recurring revenue, supporting resilient cash generation through the cycle.

Operating cash flow covers gross interest expense multiple times over, and the company's interest coverage ratio sits comfortably above the sector median. This provides substantial capacity to absorb modest EBITDA declines or incremental debt without breaching the indicative leverage threshold.

key_risks.text: Roper's growth strategy depends on acquisitions, and the risk factors disclose that suitable candidates may not be identified, financing may not be available on acceptable terms, or integration may fail to deliver anticipated revenues and cash flows. Acquisitions involve significant cash expenditures and debt incurrences, which could pressure leverage if execution disappoints.

The debt maturity profile concentrates meaningful repayments in the next twelve months and the following year, while cash on hand is modest relative to total debt. Refinancing risk is manageable given cash flow, but the company remains exposed to interest rate movements on refinanced borrowings.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Operating cash flow comfortably exceeds gross interest expense, and the indicative cash-flow-to-debt ratio remains above the downgrade threshold. However, the ratio sits below the sector median, indicating that debt service capacity, while adequate, is less robust than peers with stronger cash conversion relative to borrowings.

Free cash flow cannot be fully assessed because capital expenditure is not tagged in the available data, which is material to evaluating cash available for debt reduction after acquisitions and shareholder distributions. Acquisitions and buybacks have absorbed substantial cash, leaving limited headroom for deleveraging absent EBITDA growth.

overall_credit_view.text: Roper presents a significant indicative financial risk profile, with net leverage above the sector median and cash-flow-to-debt below the sector median. The company retains headroom to its next leverage threshold, but a modest EBITDA decline or incremental debt would erode that cushion, warranting close monitoring of acquisition funding and shareholder returns.

The credit profile is supported by high operating margins, consistent cash generation, and a diversified software portfolio. However, the acquisition-driven strategy and concentrated near-term maturities introduce event risk. We view the outlook as stable but sensitive to leverage management, with refinancing and integration execution as key swing factors over the coming periods.

credit_strengths.text: Roper 的營收與營業利益在三年趨勢中穩步複合增長，營業利潤率遠高於資訊科技行業中位數。這反映其組合由具防禦性的垂直軟件及技術賦能產品組成，能產生高利潤率的經常性收入，支持其在週期中保持現金生成的韌性。
營運現金流覆蓋總利息支出達數倍，且公司的利息覆蓋率穩居行業中位數之上。這提供充裕能力以吸收適度的 EBITDA 下滑或增量債務，而不會觸及指示性槓桿門檻。

key_risks.text: Roper 的增長策略依賴收購，而風險因素披露可能無法識別合適候選對象、可能無法以可接受條款獲得融資，或整合可能無法實現預期收入及現金流。收購涉及重大現金支出及債務產生，若執行令人失望，可能對槓桿構成壓力。
債務到期結構將重大還款集中於未來十二個月及隨後一年，而手頭現金相對於總債務而言規模有限。鑑於現金流，再融資風險屬可控，但公司仍面臨再融資借款的利率變動風險。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 營運現金流穩健超過總利息支出，且指示性現金流對債務比率仍高於降級門檻。然而，該比率低於行業中位數，表明債務償付能力雖屬充足，但相較於現金轉換對借款比率更強的同行，其穩健程度較低。
自由現金流無法全面評估，因可用數據中未標示資本支出，而這對評估收購及股東分派後可用於減債的現金至關重要。收購及回購已吸收大量現金，在缺乏 EBITDA 增長的情況下，去槓桿空間有限。

overall_credit_view.text: Roper 呈現顯著的指示性財務風險狀況，淨槓桿高於行業中位數，而現金流對債務比率低於行業中位數。公司對其下一槓桿門檻仍保有緩衝空間，但適度的 EBITDA 下滑或增量債務將侵蝕該緩衝，因此值得密切監察收購融資及股東回報。
信用狀況受到高營業利潤率、持續現金生成及多元化軟件組合的支持。然而，收購驅動策略及集中的近期到期債務帶來事件風險。我們認為前景穩定，但對槓桿管理敏感，再融資及整合執行為未來期間的關鍵擺動因素。
